positions.commentary: The speaker describes investing in IBM as an unpleasant exercise for a couple of decades because the company is now a shadow of its former self despite surviving technological shifts.
The speaker notes that holding Walmart stock for 50 years is a rare feat achieved only by the Walton family, implying it is a great business to hold long-term.
The speaker lists Alphabet (Google) as a dominant, well-entrenched business with a deep moat and high returns, but questions if it will thrive 40 years from now.
The speaker mentions Amazon as a tenant in a warehouse business with inflation-indexed leases, implying the business is sound because such large tenants are unlikely to default.
The speaker lists Microsoft as a dominant, well-entrenched business with a deep moat and high returns, but questions if it will thrive 40 years from now.
The speaker mentions that when businesses last 10, 20, 30, 40, or 50 years, the number of survivors keeps going down exponentially.

The speaker uses Coca-Cola as an example of a business that did well for 35-40 years despite being managed by 'idiot managers' who made stupid acquisitions, suggesting great performance is often due to business quality rather than manager q
The speaker states that while there could be great investments in the healthcare sector, Moderna does not fall within his circle of competence.
